### Our Substitute
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-july-1-2025.html
Passage: Matthew 27:21-22
Points:
- Barabbas was condemned to death and heard the angry mob shouting outside his prison cell.
- Instead of being led out to execution, Barabbas was unexpectedly set completely free.
- Barabbas uniquely experienced an innocent man literally dying in his place.
- This historical exchange vividly models the reality of substitutionary atonement.
- Believers share Barabbas's plight, having been freed from condemnation because Jesus died in their place.

### Will Graham Devotion: Jesus Condemned, a Murderer Set Free
Author: Will Graham
Site: Billy Graham Evangelistic Association
URL: https://billygraham.org/articles/will-graham-devotion-jesus-condemned-a-murderer-set-free
Passage: Matthew 27:15-21
Points:
- Pilate sought a customary prisoner release to avoid executing an innocent man.
- Influenced by religious leaders, the assembled crowd demanded the release of a notorious murderer.
- Barabbas faced certain capital punishment before receiving an unearned pardon.
- Jesus likely took the very cross that had been reserved for Barabbas.
- Every sinner stands in Barabbas's place and is offered eternal redemption through Christ's substitution.

### Barabbas and Me
Author: David Mathis
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/barabbas-and-me
Passage: Luke 23:13-25
Points:
- Luke repeatedly underscores Christ's absolute innocence through multiple statements from Pilate.
- In stark contrast, Barabbas is highlighted as undeniably guilty of rebellion and murder.
- Pilate yields to the mob, handing over the innocent Savior and releasing the guilty rebel.
- Barabbas's physical release serves as the first explicit picture of substitution at the cross.
- Rather than scorning Barabbas, believers should recognize themselves as guilty sinners pardoned by grace.

### Jesus Stands Before Pilate
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/jesus-stands-pilate?mobile=off
Passage: Matthew 27:11-23
Points:
- Jewish authorities brought political accusations against Jesus so Roman law would require his execution.
- Pilate saw through their envy and offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and Barabbas.
- The crowd rejected Jesus and demanded that He be crucified instead of a known criminal.
- Pilate chose personal political expediency and peace-keeping over executing genuine justice.
- Believers must recognize God's righteous character and actively oppose injustice in society.
